labeling: Synthetic examples authored and labeled by an AI coding assistant from stated text semantics; not real incident records, not blinded labels, and not independent epidemiological validation.
scope: Development regression suite for event triage, entity attribution and geographic abstention. Disease and country expectations are explicit when unambiguous. No claims about real-world sensitivity, predictive value, lead time or WHO endorsement.

cases.text: Cholera outbreak confirmed in Kenya.
cases.rationale: Affirmative outbreak statement with one explicit country.

cases.text: Ghana reports 25 new measles cases.
cases.rationale: New case report identifies one disease and one country.

cases.text: Dengue cases surge in Bangkok, Thailand.
cases.rationale: City and country describe the same event location.

cases.text: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
cases.rationale: The full country name unambiguously identifies DR Congo.

cases.text: Nigeria confirms 12 new mpox cases.
cases.rationale: Affirmative count, explicit disease and country.

cases.text: H5N1 avian flu detected in poultry in Vietnam.
cases.rationale: Animal detections are reviewable event signals; the subtype takes precedence over its generic alias.

cases.text: Nipah outbreak reported in Bangladesh.
cases.rationale: Direct outbreak claim; review is not verification of truth.

cases.text: Yemen reports a cholera outbreak with 42 cases.
cases.rationale: The country precedes the disease but remains the sole event location.

cases.text: Lassa fever cases confirmed in Nigeria.
cases.rationale: The specific disease must suppress its overlapping short alias.

cases.text: Whooping cough outbreak confirmed in Spain.
cases.rationale: A known disease synonym should canonicalize without changing the event meaning.

cases.text: Brote de cólera confirmado en Argentina.
cases.rationale: Spanish explicitly reports a confirmed cholera outbreak.

cases.text: Épidémie de rougeole confirmée en France.
cases.rationale: French explicitly reports a confirmed measles outbreak.

cases.text: Uganda declares its Ebola outbreak over.
cases.rationale: A declaration that an outbreak is over must never become a new active alert.

cases.text: Rwanda declares the end of the Marburg outbreak.
cases.rationale: The event is explicitly ended, although the pathogen has high intrinsic severity.

cases.text: The cholera outbreak in Tanzania has ended.
cases.rationale: Past event resolution is explicit.

cases.text: Liberia declared Ebola-free after the outbreak.
cases.rationale: An Ebola-free declaration is resolution context, not transmission evidence.

cases.text: Uganda declara el fin del brote de ébola.
cases.rationale: Spanish outbreak-end declaration must retain its negating event meaning.

cases.text: Uganda declares the Ebola outbreak over. The response recorded 12 cases and four deaths.
cases.title: Uganda declares the Ebola outbreak over.
cases.rationale: Historical counts in the body do not overturn an explicit resolution headline.

cases.text: No Ebola cases have been reported in Uganda.
cases.rationale: The sentence explicitly denies the occurrence of cases.

cases.text: Kenya reports no cholera outbreak.
cases.rationale: An outbreak keyword inside a denial must not trigger review.

cases.text: Suspected Ebola case in Uganda tests negative.
cases.rationale: A negative diagnostic result resolves this suspected event against the named disease.

cases.text: Cholera ruled out after investigation in Kenya.
cases.rationale: The named disease has been explicitly ruled out.

cases.text: No se han confirmado casos de cólera en Argentina.
cases.rationale: Spanish explicitly denies confirmed cases.

cases.text: Aucun cas de choléra signalé en France.
cases.rationale: French explicitly reports absence of cases.

cases.text: Ebola vaccine trial launches in Uganda.
cases.rationale: A vaccine trial is not evidence of a current outbreak.

cases.text: Funding announced for cholera preparedness in Kenya.
cases.rationale: Preparedness funding alone does not report an event.

cases.text: Nigeria hosts training on Lassa fever surveillance.
cases.rationale: Training news is background context.

cases.text: Study reviews the 2014 Ebola outbreak in Liberia.
cases.rationale: A retrospective study does not establish present transmission.

cases.text: How to prevent dengue when traveling to Thailand.
cases.rationale: Preventive travel advice is not a report of an ill traveler.

cases.text: Travel health guide: malaria prevention for visitors to Kenya.
cases.rationale: Mentioning visitors does not imply an individual became ill.

cases.text: Uganda runs an Ebola outbreak simulation exercise.
cases.rationale: A simulated outbreak must not enter the current-event review queue.

cases.text: Workshop on measles vaccination held in Ghana.
cases.rationale: Vaccination workshop reports an activity rather than cases.

cases.text: Weekly roundup: dengue in Thailand; cholera in Kenya; mpox in Nigeria.
cases.rationale: Three independent disease-country pairs cannot be collapsed into one inferred event.

cases.text: Cholera outbreaks reported in Kenya and Tanzania.
cases.rationale: Two equally asserted event countries require abstention from a single map assignment.

cases.text: Dengue outbreak in Thailand. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-123
cases.rationale: A publisher's .co.uk domain is not an event location.

cases.text: Dengue outbreak reported. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-123
cases.rationale: A URL cannot provide a missing outbreak country; active language alone cannot be mapped.

cases.text: Measles outbreak confirmed in Ghana. https://example.org/kenya/uganda
cases.rationale: Country strings in link paths must be excluded from geographic evidence.

cases.text: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever case confirmed in Spain.
cases.rationale: Congo within a disease name must not override Spain as the event country.

cases.text: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever case confirmed.
cases.rationale: The disease name supplies no actual place of occurrence.

cases.text: Sudan virus disease outbreak confirmed in Uganda.
cases.rationale: Sudan is part of the pathogen name, while Uganda is the explicit outbreak location.

cases.text: Cholera outbreak reported in South Sudan.
cases.rationale: The full country name must prevent a false Sudan assignment.

cases.text: Measles outbreak confirmed in Guinea-Bissau.
cases.rationale: A distinct country must not be silently assigned to Guinea.

cases.text: Cholera outbreak reported in Papua New Guinea.
cases.rationale: Papua New Guinea is not Guinea.

cases.text: Measles outbreak confirmed in an unnamed district.
cases.rationale: No usable country is stated; assigning one would invent evidence.

cases.text: Cholera outbreak reported in Congo.
cases.rationale: Bare Congo does not uniquely distinguish the two sovereign countries.

cases.text: I returned from Thailand sick with fever.
cases.rationale: A first-person return plus current illness is a traveler report, without claiming a diagnosis.

cases.text: I came back from Bali sick with dengue.
cases.rationale: One destination and an explicit personal illness support traveler triage.

cases.text: If you return from Thailand with fever, seek medical advice.
cases.rationale: A conditional recommendation is not a claim that a traveler is currently ill.

cases.text: The museum in Thailand opens a new exhibition.
cases.rationale: A place name without any disease or illness event cannot become a health signal.

cases.text: New art exhibition in Spain. https://example.org/ebola
cases.rationale: A disease word present only in a URL is not evidence of disease in the article.

cases.text: Cholera - Kenya
cases.title: Cholera - Kenya
cases.rationale: A disease-country WHO DON headline warrants review without inventing explicit active event language.

cases.text: Cholera - Kenya
cases.rationale: The same bare words on social media do not establish an occurrence.

cases.text: In 2014, an Ebola outbreak caused 100 cases in Liberia.
cases.rationale: A past year and past-tense event description do not report a current event.

cases.text: Uganda conducts an exercise simulating 500 cases of Ebola.
cases.rationale: Numeric case counts in a simulation are hypothetical and cannot establish an outbreak.

cases.text: Study models 100 cases of cholera in Kenya under a hypothetical scenario.
cases.rationale: A modeled count is not an observed case count or an active event.

cases.text: Kenya confirms a cholera outbreak with 12 cases and no deaths.
cases.rationale: No deaths negates the death count, not the explicitly affirmed outbreak.

cases.text: Kenya reports 100 new cholera cases as a vaccination campaign begins.
cases.rationale: A response activity does not negate explicitly reported new cases.

cases.text: France funds cholera preparedness in Kenya.
cases.rationale: France is a funder; Kenya is the program location, and preparedness remains context.

cases.text: I returned from Thailand with no fever.
cases.rationale: Explicit absence of the only symptom must not create a sick-traveler signal.

cases.text: No Ebola cases are currently reported in Liberia. The 2014 Ebola outbreak in Liberia involved 100 cases.
cases.rationale: An explicit current denial is not overturned by a separate retrospective description.
